questions: How many chains did you build and measure at each length, and how many Cr12 chains showed zero-bias end modes? Is the Cr4 to Cr12 series one chain grown atom by atom, or separate chains?
Why were the others set aside? Sec. S6 mentions "stacking fault and rupture of the spin chains" as length increases; how many chains broke, and at which length?
Which chain lengths, bias ranges, setpoints and tips did you measure beyond the ones shown, for example Cr6, Cr7, Cr9 to Cr11, or chains longer than Cr12?
What does the second-best Cr12 chain, or the next-longest chain with end modes, look like?

The main text gives "L = 12 × 4.75 = 114 Å" (p. 3) and Sec. S5 gives "L = 12 × 4.75 = 57 Å" (p. S3). Which value gives ξM ≃ 10.5 Å? With 57 Å and cos(kF L) = 1 I get about 11 Å, and with 114 Å about 24 Å. And since 10.5 Å is about 2.2 spacings of 4.75 Å, how did you count "three lattice sites"?
Which Rashba coupling did Figs. 2(b), 3 and 4 use: "αR ≈ 1.8 eV·Å" (p. S1) or "αR = 3.6 eV-Å" (p. S2)? Which one gives the 16.8 µeV splitting?
In Fig. S1(a), does the weaker end state sit at the same bias as the stronger one within your resolution, and is a deliberate defect at one end feasible?
Is the "Cr ∗ 12" chain of the RF measurement (p. 4) the same chain as in Fig. 4, and what does the asterisk mark?
